name: Fire and gas detection systems
applications: process areas with flammable or toxic inventory
principle: Fire and gas detection senses hazardous conditions and initiates alarms and executive actions (deluge, shutdown, isolation, ventilation changes) through dedicated safety logic. Point gas detectors (catalytic, infrared, electrochemical), open-path infrared lines, ultrasonic gas leak detectors for high-pressure releases, flame detectors (UV/IR, multispectral), and smoke or heat detection in buildings are placed from coverage mapping rather than guesswork — modern practice models 3D coverage of each head against leak scenarios. The F&G system is usually SIL-rated and integrated with, but independent from, the process SIS.

process_steps.name: Detectors sense gas, flame, smoke or heat
Voting logic confirms the hazard (2oo3, 2ooN) to reject spurious trips
Executive actions started: alarm, deluge, ESD, ventilation
Detector coverage mapped and optimised against leak scenarios

limitations: detector placement is scenario-dependent; a detector that meets a spacing rule may still miss the release that matters
poisoning, fouling and dirty optics degrade gas and flame detectors silently without a test regime
advantages: the first automated response to a leak — seconds matter before escalation
3D coverage mapping turns detector layout from folklore into evidence
